He struck his face with his hands and said: "Who is so bold as to stand against the great apostle Muhammad, my mother's brother?"
He said this and called out to the whole multitude of the heathen. They set out, as many as the sand, and he came to the land of Argveti, and they surrounded the forest and the plains,
the mountains and the hills. The Christian people were shut in by the hand of the heathen: some hid in the forests and some were slaughtered.
David and Constantine, and some others of their followers, were captured.
Then, when their capture was reported to him, he raised his hands and greatly glorified his mother's brother Muhammad and his law, for his victory.
And when they had encamped, he sat upon a throne, and they brought David and Constantine before the Deaf, and presented them, bound, to that lawless one.
And for the confession of Christ these saints were martyred and endured many tortures, and afterwards they cast them into the lake,
and the torturers themselves fled, terrified by the voice that was heard from heaven on behalf of those holy martyrs. Then the godless one did not take it upon himself [?].
And when he learned that the kings of Kartli and all their kin had gone to Egrisi, and from there had moved on again to Abkhazia, he followed in their track
and destroyed all the cities and fortresses of the land of Egrisi.
And he destroyed the fortress with three walls, which is Tsikhegoji, and he passed through the wall that was the boundary of Klisura. And at the time of his coming the catholicos was Tabor.
And when the Deaf passed through Klisura, which at that time was the border between Greece and Georgia, he also destroyed Tskhumi, the city of Apsileti.
And he laid siege to the fortress of Anakopia, in which is the icon of the all-holy Mother of God, painted not by human hand but from above,
concerning which no one knows where it came from. It was found on the top of that hill, which is bounded on the south by the sea and on the north by a forest [?].
There at that time were the kings of Kartli, Mir and Archil; their father had died and been buried in Egrisi.
And the emperor's eristavi Leon had gone into the fortress of Sobghisi, which is at the pass into Ossetia.
And no one was able to fight the Deaf, for his troops were greater and more numerous than the forests of Egrisi.
And this same Deaf seized and martyred the holy David and Constantine, whose martyrdom their Life relates to us at length.
And let us take up our earlier account. Then, while they were in that fortress of Anakopia, Murvan the Deaf came there and began to fight against those kings.
Then Archil said to his brother Mir: "This fortress-city is doomed to be destroyed.
And if they take us captive, they will search out all the hidden treasures which we buried in our land,
the possessions of Mirian the God-enlightened, and also of Vakhtang the God-enlightened king, and of all their children, which they left to us.
And he will also demand what King Heraclius hid, the full inventory of which we placed together with the two crowns of emerald and crimson ruby,
which our father, the great king Vakhtang, brought from India and Sind.
We buried it at Ujarma, nearby, between the two unguarded towers, and all of it is recorded in my mind.
And you carried away the two crowns of gold and carbuncle, one of King Mirian and one of Vakhtang,
which the king of the Persians sent as a gift to Vakhtang, together with all the gold and silver that he loaded onto five hundred pack animals and two thousand mules;
and you and our father deposited them at Kutaisi and at Tsikhegoji. But I put away my crowns and the charters of captivity [?] by myself.
Now, if we die, all that treasure will remain unknown; and when the Greeks come out, the emperor will make a search for our kin, and will give them the kingship and that treasure as well.
"So now let us not be the cause of the devastation of Kartli and of Greece. Instead let us go out and fight them on this side, toward the sea.
And if God wills, one will chase a thousand, and two will chase ten thousand."
And they went before the holy icon of the all-holy Mother of God. They bowed down to it, falling prostrate, and said:
"We go out in hope of your Son, our God, who was born of you. Offer intercession to him for us, and let your mercy go with us."
And they had with them a small number of their household troops and of the kin of the eristavis and patiakhshes, only about a thousand, and two thousand fighting men from the Abkhazian forces.
And before dawn the Lord sent wrath upon the Saracens, upon the people, their camp and their wagons. For the Abyssinian people were camped on the river
that is called the Abasha, while the pack animals[?] and the wagons were on the bank of the river that is called the Tskhenistsqali.
And signs appeared from on high, thunder and lightning, and a scorching heat of [?]. And he struck them with a bloody flux.
And that night an angel of the Lord appeared to Archil and said to him:
"Go out and fight the Hagarenes, for I have sent upon them a plague that cruelly destroys, from man to beast.
And when you go out, you will hear from their camp a sound of lamentation and weeping. But be brave and grow strong in hope of God."
And as dawn was breaking, a sound of weeping and wailing was heard from their camp.
Then they went out in hope of God to do battle with them. They fought, and the Lord gave victory to the small Christian force.
And thirty-five thousand of the Saracens perished from the flux, and three thousand by the sword.
And Mir was wounded in the side by a spear. Of the Christians, sixty men were killed that day. The Saracens' horses fell like a thicket, and they threw them all into the sea.
Then a certain Hagarene saw a vision, in which it seemed their prophet was saying to him:
"God has given us victory until ten kings have reigned and passed, as God said to Abraham and to Hagar;
but keep away from the holy churches and from God-serving men, as I commanded you in my Quran." They quickly set out and turned back the way they had come.
And when they had passed Tsikhegoji, they camped on those two rivers, which are alike. Heavy rain came down, and the rivers rose violently.
And the smaller river fell upon the army of the Abyssinians and carried away twenty-three thousand [?] of them.
And the larger river fell upon the horsemen, whose camp was in the riverside meadow. Some of them fled the place and some climbed up into trees, and it carried away thirty-five thousand horses.
And from that time those two rivers have been named: one Tskhenistsqali ("horse-water") and the other Abasha.
And when Marwan the Deaf saw all this that had come upon him, he greatly blamed himself and his advisers for having come into this narrow and wooded land.
He set out and camped at Pitiota, on the seashore, the city which is called Tskhumi. From there he broke camp and went round by the road through Guria.

And they passed through Speri, and because of their great numbers no loss could be seen. But before that they had cut off their horses' tails, because the horses could not drag themselves out of the mud.
And the godless Marwan the Deaf passed down along the seacoast. He took the fortresses and cities of the coast and left the whole coastal land desolate and impassable,
until he reached the city that is Constantinople. They made camp at the place called Chalcedon, because the sea there runs narrow and has no breadth.
So the senseless and witless Deaf One decided to fill the sea with stones and make it passable, so that he could lead his army across the sea on foot and in this way take the city of Constantinople.
But God brought his plan to nothing, and the wrath of God overtook him: he lay down in the evening in good health, and at dawn he was found dead, loathed and forgotten by all.
When his troops saw this, they scattered and fled back to their own land.
At that time the land of Kartli, Armenia and Ran had been ruined. No buildings could be found any longer, and there was no food at all for people or for animals.
Mir, Archil and Leon, the eristavi (duke) of Abkhazia, sent an envoy to the king of the Greeks and told him all that God had done by their hands.
He sent two crowns and a charter to Mir and Archil, and wrote to them with it: "Kingship, courage and wisdom in Kartli have been yours.
Now, although you are persecuted along with us for serving the Cross, when we are restored, as God has promised us, you will be glorified together with us.
But stay in your strongholds until their three hundred years have passed;
for in the two hundred and fiftieth year their kingdom will decline [?], and when the three hundredth year is complete, power will be given to our kingdom.
"and let us crush the Hagarenes, and all their exalted ones will be humbled, and those who give glory together with us will be exalted." And he wrote to Leo in this way:
"Throughout all the borders of Kartli harm has been done by us, while their kings have given us support and benefit.
Now this is the third service and benefit they have rendered to this royal throne of ours. First,
they received baptism under our hand. Next, they saved the great city of Pontus from destruction, and they made peace between us and the Persians.
For that same King Vakhtang acted as mediator, and with his sword he won back Palestine and two parts of Jazira (Mesopotamia) for this kingdom.
Now, if God had not checked that wicked enemy through them, he would have come all the way to Constantinople.
God made them distinguished among the sons of Nimrod, for their race has never lacked wise and discerning men and warriors,
as the written charter tells us, in which the kings are recorded, distinguished by their tribes and their lands.
As for you, I have granted the eristavate (duchy) of Abkhazia to you, your sons and your descendants forever.
But give due honour to the kings and peoples of Kartli. From now on you shall have no power to harm them or their borders in Egrisi, whether they remain there or depart from there."
Mir's wound grew worse and he came near death. He said to his brother Archil: "See, brother, I am going to our fathers.
But take me and bury me in the tomb with our fathers, and I will tell you where the place of our hidden treasures is.
"And I have no son or grandson as heir; instead I have seven daughters. Now you are the heir of the house of our kingship, the house of King Mirian.
"And you know yourself that we have not given a daughter, a child of ours, as a wife to our eristavis.
"Instead, we gave them to kings, or to someone who came from among the Persians and was of royal kin, like
"Peroz, to whom King Mirian gave his daughter as a wife. And we have been reduced, for you have no wife, and I have no son.
"Now, since our fathers married the daughters of our eristavis, give my daughters to them and divide the lands of Kartli among them:
"half to you and half to them. And I have given you what I held as the senior's portion, and you shall hold it as the senior's portion: Egrisi, Svaneti, Takveri, Argveti and Guria.
"But give Klarjeti and the central highlands to my daughters, so that they may live there during these evil times.
"And our father also died in this turmoil, and we could not take him to Mtskheta. Send his bones away and bury them in the church of Kutaisi,
"so that it may stand as a witness to our inheritance. And you stay here and look to the Greeks for help until this darkness passes."
And Mir died, and they brought him to Mtskheta and buried him in the upper church, at the entrance of the gate. And his brother Archil took his place as king.
The forty-fourth king, Archil, son of King Stephen and brother of King Mir, a Khosroid. And Archil summoned the eristavis of Kartli and gave them his brother's daughters:
the first he gave to his father's brother's son, the son of Guaram the kouropalates, who held Klarjeti and Javakheti;
the second he gave to the patiakhsh, a kinsman of Peroz, who ruled Trialeti, Tashiri and Abotsi;
the third he gave to Nerse of the Nersianids, who had been a nobleman of King Vakhtang;

the fourth he gave to Adarnase of the Adarnasianids, and between these two he divided the Upper Country, which is Kartli. The fifth he gave to Varzman, and gave him the land from Kotmani to Kurdis-Khevi.
This Varzman was a kinsman of the Persian eristavi of Bardav, who was King Vakhtang's mother's father.
The sixth he gave to Juansher of the Juansherids, who was a kinsman of King Mirian, of the descendants of Rev. And he gave him Jvari and Kherki, all of Mtiuleti, the Manglisi valley and Tbilisi.
And Archil's own share was made up of scattered pieces set apart from all these valleys.
And when the others saw that he had given the larger share to Juansher, they were somewhat displeased.
And he sent these princes away with their wives, each to his own place. And Archil summoned Leon and said:
"May you be blessed by the Lord, for you looked after us well while we were your guests, and you kept us in peace in your lands.
"But now [?] the rebuilding of our lands from Klisura upward [is needed]. I am going to settle in Tsikhe-Goji and Kutaisi.
"Now ask what you want from me for yourself, in return for your good service."
And Leon said: "The emperor has given me this land as a hereditary possession, thanks to your valour.
"And from now on it is my patrimony and inheritance, from Klisura to the great river of Khazaria, where the end of this Caucasus reaches."
Count me too among your servants, whom you have today made worthy to be your sons and brothers.
I do not want a portion from you; rather, let what is mine also be yours." Then he gave Leon his niece Guranduxt (his brother's daughter) as a wife, and the crown which
the king of the Greeks had sent for Mir. And they made a covenant and a fearful oath that there would be no enmity between them, but that Leon would defer to Archil all his days.
Archil set out and settled in Egrisi as far as Shorapani. He set all the fortresses and cities in order, and he built a fortress on the border between Guria and the land of the Greeks.
Twelve years passed in these affairs, and Kartli began to be rebuilt.
But Mtskheta was too ruined to live in. Archil came down from Egrisi and settled at the ruined fortress of Khidari.
Then a certain prince came to him who was of the lineage of David the prophet, named Adarnase, the nephew of Adarnase the Blind,
whose father had been related by marriage to the Bagratids and had been appointed by the Greeks as eristavi of the regions of Somkhiti.
During the captivity under the Deaf One he had gone down to Klarjeti with the sons of Guaram the curopalates, and had remained there.
He made a request of Archil and said: "If you are willing to treat me as one of your own settled subjects, give me land." And he gave him Shulaveri and Artani.

After this Archil came to Kakheti. He granted Kakheti to all the members of his household and made them aznauris (nobles). He built a church at Sadzmori, and he married the daughter of Guaram the curopalates,
who was one of the descendants of King Vakhtang born of his Greek wife. He settled in Tsukheti and built a palace, and he built a fortress in the valley of Lakuasti.
In Tsukheti he found princes to whom King Vakhtang had granted Tsukheti.
At that time there was a man named Abukhuasro who was eristavi over the Tush, the Khunz and all the pagans of that mountain region, and Archil did not wish to take Tsukheti from him.
And he built a fortified city at Nukhpati, between two rivers.
The people of Nukhpati had formerly been pagans with the nature of wild beasts, but the Deaf One had destroyed most of them. And Archil baptized them by force.
The Saracens had grown strong in the land of Ran. They had seized Gaziri and Somkhiti, and Maslama was at war with the Greeks.
Meanwhile the nephews of Adarnase the Blind, three brothers, came from Taron to Shakikh. It was their paternal uncle whose eyes had been put out.
They settled there by Archil's command, for the whole side of the Caucasus toward Ran had been left without inhabitants.
As for Hereti and Kakheti, only what lay in the river thickets and forests had survived. All three brothers settled there, as far as Gulgula.
At that same time certain patiakhshes did not get along in Klarjeti. Half of them went elsewhere, seized a crag in Tao called Kalmakhi, and built it into a fortress.
The other half came to Archil in Kakheti.
He gave one of them a wife from the kin of Abukhuasro, for she had been widowed and had no husband. And he granted him Tsukheti together with its fortress and palace.
During that period the Saracens held back from entering Kartli for fifty years after the departure of the Deaf One.
Up to this time they no longer came in, but received tribute from the eristavis.
And Archil had two sons, Juansher and John, and four daughters: Guarandukht, Mariam, Mirandukht and Shushan.
This Martyrdom of Archil, and the Life of the Kings, and the Conversion of Kartli by Nino were written down by Leonti Mroveli.
